title: Two Values Were Swapped in a Search Tree

concept.title: In the in-order list a swap leaves one or two places where the order goes down
body: The in-order walk of a binary search tree gives the values in increasing order. If **two values are swapped**, the in-order list is almost sorted: it has exactly one or two places where a value is **larger than the next one** (a "descent").

- If the swapped values are neighbours in the list (`... 3 [5 4] 6 ...` becomes `... 3 5 4 6 ...`... or similar), there is **one** descent, and the two values around it are the swapped nodes.
- Otherwise there are **two** descents; the first node of the **first** descent and the second node of the **second** descent are the swapped ones (the big value moved to the left, the small value moved to the right).

body.code:
first = second = prev = None
stack, node = [], root
while stack or node:                      # an iterative in-order walk
    while node:
        stack.append(node)
        node = node.left
    node = stack.pop()
    if prev and prev.val > node.val:      # a descent
        if first is None:
            first = prev                  # the first descent gives the first node
        second = node                     # the last descent gives the second node
    prev = node
    node = node.right
first.val, second.val = second.val, first.val

body: Both swapped nodes are found in one in-order walk; the values are then swapped back, and the shape of the tree never changes. (Another way: collect all nodes in in-order, sort their values, and write them back: O(n log n).)

statement: Exactly two nodes of a binary search tree had their values swapped. Swap them back, so that the tree is a binary search tree again (only values change, the shape stays). Print the recovered tree in level order in the same form as a tree in the input (`N` for a missing child, no `N` at the end).
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
outputFormat: The recovered tree in level order on one line.
constraints: -10^9 <= every value <= 10^9, and all values are different
The height of the tree is at most 800.
The tree was a binary search tree before exactly two of its values were swapped.

examples.note: The values 1 and 3 were swapped: 3 1 N N 2.

hints: The in-order list of a search tree is increasing.
After a swap, scan the in-order list for places where a value is larger than the next one.
The first node of the first such place and the second node of the last such place are the swapped nodes.

explanation: An iterative in-order walk finds the descents of the in-order list: the first node of the first descent and the second node of the last descent are the swapped nodes, and their values are swapped back.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))


def recover(root):
    first = second = prev = None
    stack = []
    node = root
    while stack or node is not None:
        while node is not None:
            stack.append(node)
            node = node.left
        node = stack.pop()
        if prev is not None and prev.val > node.val:
            if first is None:
                first = prev
            second = node
        prev = node
        node = node.right
    first.val, second.val = second.val, first.val

t = int(input())
vals = input().split()

root = build_tree(vals)
recover(root)
print_tree(root)
